instruction.text: Work out the volume of this object. Each cube has a volume of 1 `m`³.
Sasha’s water bottle has a capacity of 750 ml. She drinks 210 ml. Work out the volume of water left in her bottle.
instruction.sound: Sasha’s water bottle has a capacity of 750 millilitres. She drinks 210 millilitres. Work out the volume of water left in her bottle.

instruction.text: Cornelius is making a jug of lemonade to sell at his lemonade stand. The jug has a capacity of 2 `l`. He adds 450 `ml` of lemon juice. Work out the volume of water he can add in litres.
instruction.sound: Cornelius is making a jug of lemonade to sell at his lemonade stand. The jug has a capacity of 2 litres. He adds 450 millilitres of lemon juice. Work out the volume of water he can add in litres.

atoms.a: Next, subtract the volume of lemon juice from the capacity of the jug.

instruction.text: Match the object with its estimated capacity.
Match the object with its estimated volume.

Evelyn has made a pot of soup. The capacity of the pot is 3 `l` and she has filled it to the brim. One soup bowl has a capacity of 300 `ml`. She says that she has made twelve bowls of soup, is she correct?
instruction.sound: Evelyn has made a pot of soup. The capacity of the pot is 3 litres and she has filled it to the brim. One soup bowl has a capacity of 300 millilitres. She says that she has made twelve bowls of soup, is she correct?

instruction.text: Work out how many bowls of soup she has made.

atoms.a: Next, divide the capacity of the pot by the capacity of the soup bowl.
